body.executive_summary: The sample is an unsigned 64-bit Windows DLL loader, classified as malware at High severity and attributed to the Latrodectus loader family at 0.80 confidence. The single most important risk is the intact command-and-control path: two hardcoded HTTPS endpoints would deliver tasking and further payloads on any host with egress, and this run recorded no contact, no download and no registered persistence, so the quiet telemetry reflects a gated or unexercised execution rather than a benign one. Containment should proceed on the assumption of compromise: isolate every host that loaded the DLL, block titnovacrion.top and skinnyjeanso.com at DNS and egress, and hunt for the %APPDATA%\Custom_update install and its logon-triggered task before returning hosts to service.

key_findings.text: The sample is an unsigned 60,928-byte 64-bit Windows DLL with no packer signatures and only five static imports from KERNEL32.dll and USER32.dll, while 164 embedded values resolve to Windows functions and modules across roughly ten DLLs, so the API surface is rebuilt at run time rather than imported [ev_0001, ev_0003, ev_0004, ev_0008, ev_0020].

52 of 75 engines flag the file as malicious under 47 distinct labels, several naming Latrodectus and adjacent loader families, and the sandbox records 'Family: Latrodectus loader' and 'Latrodectus Loader variant 2' alongside an unsigned-PE signature, giving a family attribution of 0.80 confidence [ev_0018, ev_0014].

The sample's only transport is a hardcoded web channel to https://titnovacrion.top/live/ and https://skinnyjeanso.com/live/, decoded at run time from rolling-XOR .data blobs and used with form-urlencoded POST/GET requests, Mozilla/IE and curl user agents, and bodies that are RC4-encrypted and base64-encoded [ev_0019, ev_0008].

Tasking handling is implemented end to end: the check-in string carries counter, type, guid, os, arch, username, group, version, up and direction, the reply parser recognises URLS, URLS|<id>|<url>, COMMAND, CLEARURL and ERROR tokens, and the command set runs cmd.exe discovery - ipconfig /all, systeminfo, nltest /domain_trusts, net view /all /domain, net group "Domain Admins" /domain, whoami /groups and a WMIC AntiVirusProduct query - with each output keyed for upload [ev_0019].

Persistence material is visible in the decoded strings: Custom_update, Update_%x, Updater, LogonTrigger, rundll32.exe and the Explorer Shell Folders registry path, consistent with a self-copy placed under %APPDATA%\Custom_update and a task registered with a logon trigger through the COM Task Scheduler API [ev_0019].

Platform detection is mixed and must not be read as a clean bill: capa records eight capabilities including PEB access, obfuscated stackstrings, CRC32 hashing and RC4 PRGA, and five of the seven Sigma hits are process or LOLBin rules matching the observed rundll32-ordinal launch, while 31 YARA rules returned zero hits, two yara_scan calls failed, and the two remaining Sigma hits (a publicly accessible RDP service and failed authentications from out-of-scope countries) are environment-level findings unrelated to the DLL [ev_0007, ev_0008, ev_0009].

Nothing in the run executed to network effect: no files were dropped, no command-and-control channel was recorded, the two hardcoded C2 endpoints were never contacted, and the four observed processes are the sample's two rundll32 instances together with svchost.exe and SecurityHealthHost.exe [ev_0012, ev_0015, ev_0016, ev_0017].

Two attribution limits remain: the second rundll32 process is a child of the first, but its command line duplicates the harness invocation byte-for-byte including the .dll,#1 token, so the self-relaunch reading is held below 0.6 confidence, and the launcher token decodes as init -zzzz="%s\%s" under one scheme versus init -="%s\%s" under emulation, an unresolved discrepancy [ev_0012, ev_0019, ev_0021].

body.intro_background:
The sample is a 60,928-byte Windows PE image, md5 71d29d71641017e51b3685ce2f417796, sha1 e456eb06758c7349a3636c15c91e1a9c30bb7927, sha256 6091f2589fef42e0ab3d7975806cd8a0da012b519637c03b73f702f7586b21ef, imphash db7aeb75528663639689f852fd366243 [ev_0001][ev_0002]. The platform records it under category executable [ev_0001]; the PE header is DLL-flagged — machine 34404 (x64), five sections, four exports, linker 14.0, export-directory name UpdaterTag.dll, highest section entropy 6.48 in .data, no packer signature — and the file is unsigned [ev_0003][ev_0004]. Its complete static import surface is five functions from KERNEL32.dll and USER32.dll; the networking and ntdll functions the code uses are absent from the import directory and are resolved by name hash at run time instead [ev_0004][ev_0020].

One tool emitted a packed: true boolean during the run; that boolean is unsupported and is not carried into this report — its only hit is the MSVC Rich-header marker, while the parser records no packer signature [ev_0004][ev_0139]. We assess the obfuscation in this file is applied to strings and to API names rather than to the code image itself [ev_0020][ev_0021].

The platform classifies the artifact as a loader; the Latrodectus family name is source-derived. VirusTotal reports 52 of 75 engines as malicious with 47 distinct labels clustering as Latrodectus-, IcedId/Banker- and Ulise-named [ev_0018], and the sandbox signature engine reports Detect larodectus Loader variant 2 and Family: Latrodectus loader [ev_0014]. Those are third-party attributions carried as context; the capabilities asserted below are the ones the code and the decoded configuration establish.

Two properties of the file shape the evidence base. All operational text is stored in .data as encoded, length-prefixed blobs and decoded in memory at run time: 81 strings were recovered by emulation [ev_0019] and 101 texts by static decoding of the same region [ev_0021]. The import table is deliberately thin — five static entries [ev_0004] against 164 embedded values that resolve to Windows functions and modules across about ten libraries, including wininet, shell32, advapi32, urlmon, shlwapi, ole32, iphlpapi and ntdll [ev_0020] — with the PE-export walker and PEB access independently flagged by capa at 0x869c and 0x8690 [ev_0008]. Raw scans are consequently near-empty: 218 extracted strings [ev_0005], no IOCs [ev_0006], no match from the run's 31-rule YARA corpus [ev_0007], and from a separate file analyzer only two generic markers — CRC32_poly_Constant at 0x5f0c and win_mutex at 0xcd72, neither a family rule [ev_0144][ev_0252]. Those negatives are scope-limited, not exculpatory.

Decoding and decompilation establish a loader with a web-command channel. Two HTTPS endpoints are decoded at run time, https://titnovacrion.top/live/ and https://skinnyjeanso.com/live/ [ev_0019][ev_0021]; the decoded string set supplies the request side (POST and GET, Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the MSIE-style user agent, curl/7.88.1) [ev_0021] and the reply vocabulary URLS, URLS|%d|%s, COMMAND, CLEARURL, ERROR [ev_0019][ev_0021]. It also carries the cmd.exe command set with its per-command upload keys — /c systeminfo, /c ipconfig /all, /c net config workstation, /c net view /all and /all /domain, /c nltest /domain_trusts and /all_trusts, /c net group Domain Admins /domain, /c whoami /groups, and a WMIC AntiVirusProduct query paired with &net_wmic_av= — plus install and update templates (Custom_update, Update_%x, %s%d.exe, %s%d.dll, files/bp.dat, update_data.dat), the rundll32 relaunch templates, a Task Scheduler registration chain keyed on LogonTrigger, the single-instance mutex name runnung, and the rename/delete-on-close string :wtfbbq [ev_0019][ev_0021]. An output-capturing cmd.exe execution routine is decompiled in the code [ev_0131][ev_0202], and capa independently asserts obfuscated stackstrings, RC4 PRGA encryption, CRC32 and FNV hashing, PE-export parsing and PEB access [ev_0008], matching the string decoder, the hashed API table and the RC4-plus-base64 pair built on the runtime-decoded key 12345 and the standard base64 alphabet [ev_0021]. No embedded payload was found by the run's carving and embedded-PE checks [ev_0255][ev_0256].

The 600-second dynamic run did not exercise the loader. The sandbox process table holds four processes — two rundll32.exe entries plus host svchost.exe and SecurityHealthHost.exe — with no dropped files and no channels [ev_0012][ev_0015][ev_0016]; its network record holds 3 hosts, 5 TCP and 1 UDP flow [ev_0013]; the 587-second capture contains 9,087 packets over 17 external conversations, none at a regular interval [ev_0017], and its DNS extract contains no query for either decoded domain [ev_0021][ev_0235]. The one sample-linked execution event is the load itself: rundll32.exe C:\Users\Admin\AppData\Local\Temp\6091f2589fef42e0ab3d7975806cd8a0da012b519637c03b73f702f7586b21ef.dll,#1, an ordinal-export call that the LOLBin table maps to T1218.011 and Sigma flags as a DLL call by ordinal via rundll32 [ev_0009][ev_0011][ev_0012][ev_0214]. A second rundll32 process appears in that table with the same recorded command line; the sample contains rundll32 relaunch templates, but the record does not establish that process's origin and this report does not attribute it to them [ev_0012][ev_0019][ev_0021][ev_0214]. Because the sample's own init chain includes anti-analysis gates and a 180-second pre-beacon delay [ev_0088][ev_0174][ev_0181][ev_0191], we assess that it did not reach its C2 stage in this environment — the inert run is not evidence that C2, tasking, download or persistence are absent from the file.

Two caveats apply throughout. Negative results are coverage-limited: several tool calls failed during the run, and the dynamic record is empty for API, registry, mutex, task and file-write events for every process [ev_0210][ev_0211][ev_0212][ev_0213][ev_0225], so an unobserved behaviour is not an absent one. Third-party material also stays third-party: the family labels [ev_0018][ev_0014] and the engine verdicts on the decoded C2 domains (titnovacrion.top 16/91 and its /live/ URL 18/91; skinnyjeanso.com 19/91 and its /live/ URL 21/91) [ev_0232][ev_0233][ev_0241][ev_0244] are reported as sourced context. The report publishes the techniques the code supports — obfuscation and dynamic API resolution [ev_0008], rundll32 execution (T1218.011) [ev_0011], web-protocol C2 with symmetric encryption and standard encoding [ev_0008][ev_0021], and Windows discovery and command execution [ev_0019][ev_0021] — together with the persistence, deletion and exfiltration paths traced in the sections that follow, and it separates code-level capability from observed behaviour throughout.

payloads.body:
**No carried payload.** The sample is one 60,928-byte DLL [ev_0001], [ev_0004], and no second stage is embedded in it: carving returned 0 payloads and four independent checks for a hidden or encrypted embedded PE (8- and 16-bit string, split-data, bitmap, encrypted-PE) were negative, matching the analysis's "no embedded PE file" [ev_0255], [ev_0252]; the signature scan recorded only the sample's own `MZ\x90\x00` at offset 0 [ev_0256], and the PE analysis reports no resource directory and no overlay [ev_0083]. Carve methods are not exhaustive, so this bounds the search rather than excluding a carried stage, but no section of the module is a second binary [ev_0004]. The file is a DLL submitted under an `.exe` name, and its install routine, if reached, copies the running image into `%APPDATA%\Custom_update\Update_%x.<ext>`, choosing the extension opposite to its real type (T1036.008) [ev_0021], [ev_0019], [ev_0182].

**No dropped files in this run.** The sandbox reported 0 dropped files [ev_0015], 0 file writes [ev_0225], no channels [ev_0016], and a four-process list of two rundll32.exe instances plus svchost.exe and SecurityHealthHost.exe [ev_0012]; the 587 s / 9,087-packet capture held no traffic attributable to the sample's pids [ev_0017]. The negative is coverage-limited — the run's per-process API and registry tables were empty [ev_0212], [ev_0213] — so "0 files" records what the harness captured, not a limit of the code.

**Download and install plumbing is code-level only.** The static import table holds five imports from KERNEL32.dll and USER32.dll only [ev_0004]; every download, file and network API in play is materialised at run time by the CRC32 resolver [ev_0020], whose entries include `urlmon.dll!URLDownloadToFileW`/`URLDownloadToFileA`, the wininet HTTP set (`InternetConnectA`, `HttpOpenRequestA`, `HttpSendRequestA`, `InternetReadFile`), `CreateFileW`/`WriteFile`/`ReadFile`, `DeleteFileW` and `CreateProcessW` [ev_0020]. The `.data` string blobs supply the fetch paths and file-name templates — `/files/`, `files/bp.dat`, `%d.dat`, `%s%d.exe`, `%s%d.dll`, `%s\%d.dll` — plus the install tokens `Custom_update`/`Update_%x` and the URL/state file `\update_data.dat`, rewritten as `URLS|%d|%s\r\n` [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. The decompiled handlers rebuild URLs as `<server>/files/<token>` and save under `%LOCALAPPDATA%\<tick>.exe|.dll` and `%APPDATA%…\files\`, and fcn.0xb4cc holds the `rundll32 <dll>,<token>` execution template over the CreateProcessW slot [ev_0125], [ev_0195], [ev_0019]; one command (0xe) takes a no-file route — download, `VirtualAlloc(0,n,0x1000,0x40)` (RWX) and a thread started on the buffer (fcn.0xb398) — the sample's reflective-load capability (T1620) [ev_0188], [ev_0195]. Nothing was fetched or written: 0 drops, no contact to either decoded endpoint, no flow owned by the sample's pids [ev_0015], [ev_0017]. We assess the run did not reach the C2 stage [ev_0212], [ev_0213].

**Process pair, no file artifacts.** The observed second rundll32 (pid 89, child of pid 83) [ev_0214] was accompanied by no installed copy, downloaded module or other on-disk artifact [ev_0015]; whether the sample spawned it remains unresolved, and neither reading makes it a dropped payload.

discovery.body:
The discovery stage runs the system's own administration tools rather than enumerating from the module's own code, and it keeps the enumeration primitives out of the import table. The import directory is a complete list of five functions in two libraries — kernel32!PeekNamedPipe, kernel32!GetLastError, kernel32!CreateMutexW and user32!MessageBeep/!MessageBoxA — and the reference catalogue's only association for those five is persistence, not discovery [ev_0004, ev_0010]. The single discovery-associated API that this run's deterministic pass counted therefore sits in the file's own name-resolution table, whose 164 values are CRC32 hashes of function and module names in ASCII and UTF-16LE form; capa marks the PEB read and export-directory walk that feed that table at 0x8690 and 0x869c [ev_0008, ev_0020]. GetComputerNameExA, GetAdaptersInfo, GetUserNameA, SHGetFolderPathW/A, CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, the Process32/Thread32 families and the FindFirstVolumeW/GetVolumeInformationW pair all stand in it [ev_0020].

Most of the enumeration is one routine at offset 0x2200 (decompiled as FUN_1360bc02200). It decodes eleven (executable, command-line) pairs from the sample's XOR-rolling blobs (scheme 'xor8_rolling_header layout seed (4), text length (2), text, seed 0x33629d40, first_key 0x41', with the command text held as UTF-16LE) [ev_0021] and hands each pair to the launcher at 0x1030: ten pairs name C:\Windows\System32\cmd.exe and one names C:\Windows\System32\wbem\wmic.exe. The command lines are /c ipconfig /all, /c systeminfo, /c net config workstation, /c net view /all, /c net view /all /domain, /c nltest /domain_trusts, /c nltest /domain_trusts /all_trusts, /c net group \"Domain Admins\" /domain, /c whoami /groups, the cmd-hosted 'wmic.exe /node:localhost /namespace:\\root\SecurityCenter2 path AntiVirusProduct Get DisplayName | findstr /V /B /C:displayName || echo No Antivirus installed', and the wmic-hosted '/Node:localhost /Namespace:\\root\SecurityCenter2 Path AntiVirusProduct Get * /Format:List' [ev_0019, ev_0021]. Each child's output is concatenated behind a fixed field name — &ipconfig=, &systeminfo=, &net_config_ws=, &net_view_all=, &net_view_all_domain=, &domain_trusts=, &domain_trusts_all=, &net_group=, &whoami_group=, &wmic=, &net_wmic_av= — into one URL-encoded body fragment (the same handler's strings include 'POST' and 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded') [ev_0019, ev_0021]. The finished fragment is cached in the global at 0x1360bc10548 and returned through the caller's out-parameter, so the eleven commands are prepared at most once per process, the build path being guarded by a null-check on that global.

The launcher at 0x1030 is the child-process engine. It allocates a 0x2800-byte (10,240) accumulation buffer, creates three pipes under one inheritable SECURITY_ATTRIBUTES (nLength 0x18, bInheritHandle 1), fills a STARTUPINFO whose cb is 0x68 and whose dwFlags it ORs with 0x101 (STARTF_USESHOWWINDOW|STARTF_USESTDHANDLES), zeroes a 0x18-byte PROCESS_INFORMATION, and calls through the hash-resolved slot at 0x1360bc10b38; kernel32/kernelbase!CreateProcessW is among the resolved names and we assess that slot is it [ev_0020]. The child's pipe output is read in 0x200-byte chunks, null-terminated and appended through the helper at 0xb984; the routine then polls the child's status through another slot, compares the value against 0x103 (259, STILL_ACTIVE) and calls fcn.0x0c934 with 100 while the child is still running — the same routine is called with 1000 from the entry stub, so we assess it is a millisecond sleep. PeekNamedPipe, one of the five static imports, fits this read logic [ev_0004].

Identity data is also assembled without a child process. Routine 0x7fa8 builds &mac= with the '%02x' and ':%02x' formats together with &computername=%s and &domain=%s [ev_0021]; we assess iphlpapi!GetAdaptersInfo supplies the MAC bytes and kernel32!GetComputerNameExA the name and domain values, both standing in the resolved-hash table [ev_0020]. Routine 0x5750's request parameters — counter, type, guid, os, arch, username, group, ver, up and direction — carry the same host and user identity with each beacon [ev_0019, ev_0021].

Two further enumerations are signalled only by their upload keys; the routines that build them (0x1c38 and 0x1a08) were not decompiled in this run. &proclist=[ with the fragments '\"proc\": ' and '\"subproc\": [' [ev_0021] is consistent with a process list assembled through the resolved CreateToolhelp32Snapshot, Process32FirstW/Process32NextW, Thread32First/Thread32Next, OpenProcess and VirtualQuery names [ev_0020], and &desklinks=[ [ev_0021] fits the shell-folder vocabulary — AppData, Desktop, Startup, Personal and Local AppData read under Software\\Microsoft\\Windows\\CurrentVersion\\Explorer\\Shell Folders in routine 0x7b98 [ev_0021]. A '\\*.dll' search pattern in the decoded blob set [ev_0021] and FindFirstVolumeW/GetVolumeInformationW/FindVolumeClose in the resolved table [ev_0020] point to file and volume enumeration.

Observed activity: the sandbox process record for this run lists four processes — two rundll32.exe, svchost.exe and SecurityHealthHost.exe — with no cmd.exe or wmic.exe among them [ev_0012], so the command-driven half of this stage was not observed executing and the description above rests on static artifacts. Mapping to this report's table: T1082 System Information Discovery (the systeminfo request), T1016 System Network Configuration Discovery (ipconfig /all and net config workstation), T1482 Domain Trust Discovery (nltest /domain_trusts, its /all_trusts variant and the domain views), T1069.002 Domain Groups (net group \"Domain Admins\" /domain), T1518.001 Security Software Discovery (both AntiVirusProduct queries), T1057 Process Discovery (the proclist field), T1033 System Owner/User Discovery (whoami /groups, GetUserNameA and the beacon username field), T1083 File and Directory Discovery (desklinks, the shell folders, \\*.dll), and T1027.007 Dynamic API Resolution for the name-hash table that carries all of it.

execution_flow.action: A 64-bit DLL (submitted as an .exe) is loaded through the rundll32 LOLBin: the run records pid 83 C:\Windows\system32\rundll32.exe (ppid 56) with command line rundll32.exe C:\Users\Admin\AppData\Local\Temp\6091f2....dll,#1, an ordinal export call; the LOLBin table attributes T1218.011 and Sigma flags DLL Call by Ordinal Via Rundll32.EXE and Unsigned DLL Loaded by Windows Utility.
The ordinal entry lands on the four exports extra/follower/run/scub (ordinals 1-4), all aliasing RVA 0x3ce4 to stub fcn.0x3cb4 and worker fcn.0x3868; DllMain only stores the module handle.

The worker runs anti-analysis gates before operational work: PEB access and a BeingDebugged check that aborts, a process-count threshold (75 or 50 depending on the OS id), IsWow64Process must be 0, and the single-instance mutex runnung that aborts on ERROR_ALREADY_EXISTS (0xB7).

Resolves its API surface at start-up from CRC32 name hashes (256-entry table for 0xEDB88320, export-directory walker fcn.0x869c, 90 {hash, module, slot} triples materialised into global slots); 164 embedded values resolve to about 10 DLLs against only 5 static imports, and the visible CreateMutexW/PeekNamedPipe IAT thunks have no code callers.

Decodes its operational strings from header-validated rolling-XOR blobs in .data via routine 0xae78 (4-byte seed 0x33629d40, 2-byte length XORed with the seed's low 16 bits, first key 0x41): 101 texts decode statically and 81 also by emulation.

Copies itself to %APPDATA%\Custom_update\Update_<hex>.<ext> - directory from the Shell Folders AppData path, name from wsprintfW(Update_%x), extension chosen opposite to its own type - a name/type masquerade layer beneath the export-directory name UpdaterTag.dll.

Registers persistence as a scheduled task through the COM Task Scheduler (CLSID {0F87369F-A4E5-4CFC-BD3E-73E6154572DD}, IID {4C3D624D-FDA9-49A3-B9B7-09CB3CD3F047}) with the decoded LogonTrigger registration info and RegisterTaskDefinition flag 6 (TASK_CREATE_OR_UPDATE).

Launches the registered task and exits the parent with ExitProcess(0), using the decoded templates C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\rundll32.exe %s,%s and the one-argument form in fcn.0xb4cc with the CreateProcessW call site.

The run also records a second rundll32.exe (pid 89, first seen 172 against 141) as a child of pid 83 with a byte-identical command line; whether the sample relaunched itself is not established, since the child points at the same Temp module rather than an installed copy and harness duplication is not excluded.
Start-up decodes the two hardcoded HTTPS endpoints https://titnovacrion.top/live/ and https://skinnyjeanso.com/live/ into the candidate array at 0x10568.
Keeps the URL list RC4-encrypted at %APPDATA%\Custom_update\update_data.dat, read at start-up and rewritten in the URLS|%d|%s record format when the list changes.

Beacon thread waits 180 s before first contact, then loops: iterate the URL list under the runnung mutex, build counter=%d&type=%d&guid=%s&os=%d&arch=%d&username=%s&group=%lu&ver=%d.%d&up=%d&direction=%s, RC4-encrypt the body with the runtime-decoded key 12345, base64-encode it, POST it to a /live/ endpoint, and sleep 450-599 s (1500-2099 s after C2 command 0x13).
Decrypts and tokenises the reply (URLS, URLS|%d|%s, COMMAND, CLEARURL, ERROR) and dispatches command ids 2, 3, 4, 0xc, 0xd, 0xe, 0xf, 0x11, 0x12, 0x13, 0x14 and 0x15 to their handlers.

Command 4 runs the cmd.exe builder with output capture - inheritable pipes via CreatePipe, CreateProcessW, PeekNamedPipe/ReadFile polling in 0x200-byte chunks, STILL_ACTIVE check, Sleep(0x64) - for /c systeminfo, /c ipconfig /all, /c net config workstation, /c net view /all( /domain), /c nltest /domain_trusts( /all_trusts), /c net group "Domain Admins" /domain, /c whoami /groups and the wmic AntiVirusProduct query, each paired with its upload key (&systeminfo=, &ipconfig=, &net_config_ws=, &net_view_all=, &net_view_all_domain=, &domain_trusts=, &domain_trusts_all=, &net_group=, &whoami_group=, &net_wmic_av=).

Collectors assemble host identity for the beacon: process list (&proclist=[, "proc"/"subproc"), desktop-link and DLL enumeration over shell folders (&desklinks=[), MAC (&mac=), &computername=%s, &domain=%s, username via GetUserNameA, and group as FNV("Littlehw").

Task handlers fetch and run next stages: build <server>/files/<token>, save to %LOCALAPPDATA%\<tick>.exe or .dll and %APPDATA%\...\files\, execute a fetched DLL as rundll32 <dll>,<token>, or for command 0xe download a payload, allocate RWX (VirtualAlloc 0x40) and start a thread on it; nothing is embedded in this file (0 carved payloads).

On demand, anti-forensics on its own module: rename through SetFileInformationByHandle with the decoded name :wtfbbq (class 3 FileRenameInfo then class 4 FileDispositionInfo TRUE); uninstall command 0xf deletes the installed file and module before ExitProcess(0).

The observed run never reached steady state: 0 C2 DNS or HTTP to either endpoint across the 600 s run and the 587 s / 9,087-packet capture (17 external conversations, ambient Windows Update/OCSP/CRL estate, GET-only, no regular interval), 0 dropped files, 0 executed commands, 0 registry/task/service/mutex rows and empty API telemetry for every process.

We assess the inert record has no demonstrated cause: the gates of step 3 exist in code, the run's process table lists only four processes (possibly a filtered view), and the per-process dynamic data was empty, so the run is neither proof of execution nor exculpatory.

string_resolution.body:
The DLL's linkage is deliberately thin. The import directory holds five entries from two libraries [ev_0004]; the import-name listing shows KERNEL32!PeekNamedPipe, KERNEL32!GetLastError, KERNEL32!CreateMutexW and USER32!MessageBeep, USER32!MessageBoxA (list_strings). The functions the sample actually operates with are not in that table. FUN_0x6aa4 builds the 256-entry table for the reflected CRC32 polynomial 0xEDB88320, FUN_0x869c walks IMAGE_EXPORT_DIRECTORY and returns the export whose hashed name matches, and per-block initialisers materialise {hash, module reference, destination slot} triples at start-up; capa independently asserts 'hash data with CRC32' at 0x6aa4 and 'resolve function by parsing PE exports' at 0x869c, the latter beside 'PEB access' at 0x8690 [ev_0008]. Against those five static imports, 164 embedded 32-bit values resolve to Windows function or module names across roughly ten DLLs — kernel32, user32, wininet, shell32, advapi32, urlmon, shlwapi, ole32, iphlpapi, ntdll [ev_0020].

One block can be read directly. FUN_0xa59c places 0x25 (37) triples in a stack array, every one referencing the same module-name pointer at image base + 0x10ec8, then loops calling the resolver FUN_0x869c with the module reference, the hash and 0, storing each returned pointer into the slot field (decompile_function 0x1360bc0a59c). The constants in that loop are the ones recovered as ntdll!NtAllocateVirtualMemory (0xe0762feb), ntdll!RtlGetVersion (0xb46508b5), ntdll!NtCreateThread (0xca6b0d7b), ntdll!NtQueryInformationProcess (0xa5c44c50), ntdll!NtProtectVirtualMemory (0x5c2d1a97), ntdll!LdrLoadDll (0x183679f2), ntdll!RtlFormatCurrentUserKeyPath (0x7fa58340) and thirty more ntdll entries in the same list [ev_0020]. Resolution is load-bearing, not decorative: allocation is traced through the resolved NtAllocateVirtualMemory slot and the command line is read with NtQueryInformationProcess plus ReadProcessMemory [ev_0204], [ev_0198]. The FNV routine does the same to a decoded string — FUN_0x463c decodes the blob at image base + 0xfb10 ('Littlehw') and passes it to FUN_0xc99c, storing the 32-bit result at image base + 0x10464 (decompile_function 0x1360bc0463c), matching capa's 'hash data using fnv' at 0xc99c [ev_0008], [ev_0021]. Two of the five visible imports are reported to be decoys: the CreateMutexW and PeekNamedPipe thunks carry no code cross-references, and the mutex gate and pipe polling are reached through resolved slots [ev_0114], [ev_0119].

Strings receive the same treatment. The operational text is absent from the cleartext listing: 81 of the sample's strings were recovered only by emulation inside decoder routine 0xae78 [ev_0019], and the platform's static scheme decodes 101 texts from the data sections from a header of 4-byte seed 0x33629d40, a 2-byte length XORed with the seed's low 16 bits and a first key byte of 0x41, listing the offset that refers to each [ev_0021]. Decompilation of FUN_0xae78 confirms that header read followed by a 4-byte state advanced with the helper at 0x9040 (decompile_function 0x1360bc0ae78), and an independent re-derivation reproduced the blobs byte-for-byte [ev_0168]. What comes out is the sample's configuration and tooling: the two HTTPS endpoints, the cmd.exe launch templates, the /c discovery command lines, the wmic antivirus query, the beacon format string counter=%d&type=%d&guid=%s&…, the RC4 key '12345', the standard base64 alphabet, the rundll32 relaunch templates and the ':wtfbbq' rename token [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. The blobs sit in .data, which is also the file's highest-entropy section at 6.48 [ev_0004], and capa's 'contain obfuscated stackstrings' rule fires at 0x9484 [ev_0008].

The raw-layer negatives follow from this design and are not exculpatory. A string scan sees 218 strings of length ≥6 [ev_0005], the 31-rule default corpus returns no hit [ev_0007], and the cleartext IOC scan returns nothing [ev_0006]. The recording scheme itself bounds the recovered set: text whose encoded bytes already read as printable text is not decoded unless a header states where it ends, so further encoded text may remain [ev_0021]. One token is contested between the two decoding paths — the header-validated static decode yields 'init -zzzz="%s\%s"' at 0xfac0 [ev_0021] while emulation yields 'init -="%s\%s"' at the same site [ev_0019]; the disagreement is confined to that one format string and is left unsettled. On this record the sample supports T1027 Obfuscated Files or Information (operational strings stored as encoded blobs, decoded only in memory), T1027.007 Dynamic API Resolution (no static import for the operational API surface, which is rebuilt from export-name CRC32 hashes) and T1140 Deobfuscate/Decode Files or Information (runtime decode of those blobs).

persistence_detail.body:
The run's parsed persistence view lists twelve persistence-mechanism entries, four persistence-related API references and one registry API; the API catalogue association flags a persistence behaviour [ev_0010]. The mechanism the code implements is a scheduled task registered through the COM Task Scheduler interface.

The chain is reached from the DLL's own export stub: the decompiled `sym.UpdaterTag.dll_extra` (export name `extra` [ev_0004], [ev_0083]; stub decompile [ev_0084], [ev_0086]) calls fcn.0x3cb4, which calls fcn.0x3868; fcn.0x3868 calls fcn.0x33ac, and fcn.0x33ac calls fcn.0x3728 -> fcn.0xb344 -> fcn.0xc5e8 -> fcn.0xc42c -> fcn.0xc2c4 [ev_0113], [ev_0115], [ev_0120], [ev_0123], [ev_0189]. fcn.0xc5e8 is the COM creation/connect stage, reached with CLSID {0F87369F-A4E5-4CFC-BD3E-73E6154572DD} and IID {4C3D624D-FDA9-49A3-B9B7-09CB3CD3F047}; fcn.0xc2c4 dispatches through interface vtables (offsets 0x48, 0x50, 0x10, 0xb8), applies the registration-info string `LogonTrigger` (data @0x10030, referenced at 0xc3a4) to a logon trigger, and calls RegisterTaskDefinition with flag 6 (TASK_CREATE_OR_UPDATE) [ev_0113], [ev_0196], [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. The flow then invokes the task launcher fcn.0xb400 and calls through the resolved slot at 0x1360bc10b68 with argument 0, which the code-level reading names ExitProcess(0) [ev_0113], [ev_0123], [ev_0020]. The launcher templates are `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\rundll32.exe %s,%s` and `C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\rundll32.exe %s` (data @0xfe90 / @0xfef0, referenced at 0xb555 / 0xb5af inside fcn.0xb4cc) [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. None of this sits in the static import table, which the complete DLL list limits to kernel32.dll and user32.dll [ev_0004]: ole32 CoInitializeEx/CoCreateInstance/CoInitialize are among the 164 CRC32-resolved names the binary builds at run time [ev_0020] through the PE-export parser at 0x869c, beside PEB access at 0x8690 [ev_0008].

No other autostart is traced. Registry access is a Shell Folders path resolver, not an autostart writer: fcn.0x7b98 decodes the folder names `AppData`, `Desktop`, `Startup`, `Personal`, `Local AppData` and `Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Explorer\Shell Folders` (data @0x10330, referenced at 0x7df1) [ev_0021], [ev_0019]; the resolver builds a per-user NT key prefix with RtlFormatCurrentUserKeyPath or the literal `\Registry\Machine\` prefix and opens (0x20019) and queries the value (REG_SZ) [ev_0020], [ev_0270], [ev_0274], [ev_0283], [ev_0285]. The only consumer traced is fcn.0x30d0 taking index 0 (AppData) for the install directory [ev_0270], [ev_0274], [ev_0283], [ev_0285]. Startup-folder autostart is not implemented in the code read: `Startup` is one of the folder names the resolver returns, no code path writing into Startup is traced, and the report withdraws T1547.001 [ev_0182], [ev_0195], [ev_0021]. The resolved-name table does carry shlwapi SHGetValueA/SHSetValueA and SHGetValueW/SHSetValueW [ev_0020]; no autostart value written through them is traced. Single-instance primitives (CreateMutexW/OpenMutexW/ReleaseMutex) are in the same table [ev_0020]; no mutex was observed at run time [ev_0221].

Persistence-adjacent state that does not autostart sits under `%APPDATA%\Custom_update\`: the URL list (`URLS`, data @0x103f0, ref 0xd0c4) is read and RC4-decrypted from `update_data.dat` (data @0x103b8, ref 0xced2) by fcn.0xcea4/fcn.0xcf14 [ev_0019], [ev_0021], [ev_0177], [ev_0175] and re-encrypted on change by fcn.0xd1c8 with `URLS|%d|%s\r\n` (data @0x10400, ref 0xd247) [ev_0021], [ev_0169]. The staging names `Custom_update` (ref 0x312b in fcn.0x30d0) and `Update_%x` (ref 0x31f1 in fcn.0x3194), with the path formats `%s%d.dll` / `%s%d.exe` (refs 0x6cc5 / 0x6e55), describe the drop path this reading places in that directory [ev_0021], [ev_0019]. That is configuration retention and staging, not an autostart entry.

No autostart was registered during the run: registry 0 rows, tasks/services/commands 0 rows, `executed_commands` / `created_services` / `started_services` empty, file writes 0, dropped files 0 [ev_0213], [ev_0211], [ev_0221], [ev_0225], [ev_0015]. Those negatives are coverage-limited — per-process API telemetry was empty, so a registration could run without leaving a row [ev_0212], [ev_0221]. The run's process list holds two rundll32.exe instances [ev_0012]; the launcher templates show the chain re-enters the DLL through rundll32 [ev_0021], but neither instance is tied to a task registration on this evidence, and which of the two is the sample's remains unresolved. Read with the process-count/PEB gates and the 180 s pre-beacon delay, the published reading is that the sample did not reach its C2/tasking stage in this environment, not that persistence is absent [ev_0212], [ev_0214], [ev_0017]. Confirming registration needs an instrumented run with task, registry and file telemetry [ev_0221], [ev_0227].

command_and_control.body:
Configuration. The sample's C2 configuration is two HTTPS endpoints, carried encoded in the data section and reconstructed at run time: `https://titnovacrion.top/live/` (.data+0x10250, decoder reference 0x69b3) and `https://skinnyjeanso.com/live/` (.data+0x10278, reference 0x6a1f) [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. fcn.0x6988 decodes both and writes them into the candidate slot array at 0x10568 under a byte counter, then admits a third, caller-supplied URL before writing the null terminator; we assess that third slot is where a server-pushed URL from the `URLS|%d|%s` reply is installed, making the built-in pair a bootstrap list rather than the full contact set [ev_0090], [ev_0169], [ev_0182], [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. Raw-string IOC extraction returned neither domain — cleartext-string negatives on this sample are scope-limited, and the decode-backed endpoints are the indicators of record [ev_0254], [ev_0006].

Transport. The channel is WinINet over TCP/443 (T1071.001 Web Protocols), and every network API it needs is resolved at run time by CRC32 name hashing rather than imported: the resolved hash set covers InternetOpen*, InternetConnectA, HttpOpenRequestA, HttpSendRequestA, InternetReadFile, InternetCrackUrlA and InternetSetOptionA, against only 5 static imports from kernel32/user32 [ev_0020], [ev_0004], [ev_0136], [ev_0137]. fcn.0x5030 builds the request. It decodes `Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded` (.data+0xfb68, reference 0x5076), decodes the verb from the `POST`/`GET` strings (.data+0xfba0 / 0xfbb0, references 0x5100 / 0x5180), passes the accept-type array `*/*` (.data+0xfb60) to HttpOpenRequestA through slot 0x10e10, and on the variant that carries a body passes the content-type and the body buffer to HttpSendRequestA (slot 0x10e18), while the alternate variant calls HttpSendRequestA with no headers or body [ev_0019], [ev_0021], [ev_0129], [ev_0175]. The reply is read with InternetReadFile (slot 0x10e30) [ev_0136], [ev_0137]. The same function calls InternetSetOptionA(hRequest, 0x1f, &0x4380, 4) through slot 0x10e40; 0x4380 is bit-for-bit the combination of SECURITY_FLAG_IGNORE_REVOCATION, IGNORE_UNKNOWN_CA, IGNORE_WRONG_USAGE and IGNORE_REDIRECT_TO_HTTPS, so we assess the channel is configured to proceed past certificate and redirect validation failures — a reading held at lower weight because it rests on a single decompiler locus [ev_0129], [ev_0136], [ev_0185].

Beacon and tasking. The reversing pass identifies the beacon thread as fcn.0x5750, started from fcn.0x6250 after the install branch sets a global to 2 and the non-install path sets it to 1, i.e. type = 2 on a fresh install and 1 thereafter [ev_0169], [ev_0191], [ev_0185], [ev_0175]. The check-in body is `counter=%d&type=%d&guid=%s&os=%d&arch=%d&username=%s&group=%lu&ver=%d.%d&up=%d&direction=%s` (.data+0xfd40, references 0x5b0f / 0x5bfe / 0x5d23), sent as the POST payload [ev_0019], [ev_0021]. The same pass records a 180 s (0x708 × 100 ms) wait before first contact, then jittered 450–599 s cycles that stretch to 1500–2099 s after C2 command 0x13 [ev_0191]. The identifying fields are host-derived: `group` is traced to the FNV hash of the decoded string `Littlehw` and `guid` to the volume formatter `%04X%04X%04X%04X%08X%04X` fed by FindFirstVolumeW/GetVolumeInformationW [ev_0021], [ev_0019], [ev_0109], [ev_0198]. Bodies and replies are handled by the KSA/PRGA pair that capa flags as RC4 at 0xcaac, keyed with the run-time-decoded string `12345` (.data+0xfd30) and encoded with the standard base64 alphabet (.data+0x10160) [ev_0008], [ev_0019], [ev_0021], [ev_0167], [ev_0175], [ev_0193]. Replies are tokenised on CRLF then `|` into `URLS`, `URLS|%d|%s`, `COMMAND`, `CLEARURL` and `ERROR` [ev_0019], [ev_0021], and routed to handlers (URLS|id|url → 0xccbc, CLEARURL → 0xce20, COMMAND → 0x3cf4, ERROR ignored), with the COMMAND ids 2, 3, 4, 0xc–0xf and 0x11–0x15 covering collectors, downloaders, in-memory execution, cleanup and sleep-mode changes [ev_0203], [ev_0169], [ev_0175]. No second stage is embedded: the file yields 0 carved payloads and 4 independent embedded-PE checks were negative, so tasking must be fetched [ev_0025], [ev_0142]; download URLs are assembled from the stored C2 entry up to `//` plus `/files/` (.data+0xfb00, reference 0x3ef6) and a token [ev_0021], [ev_0019], and the results reach execution through the parameterised rundll32 templates in fcn.0xb4cc or the VirtualAlloc(RWX)+thread path [ev_0195], [ev_0189], [ev_0125].

Not observed. Neither endpoint appears in any telemetry from this run. The sandbox network record has no DNS entry, no HTTP entry and no channel, and all of its flows belong to other pids (2928, 5800, 6092, 4264, 2508, 1380; the sample's processes are 83 and 89) [ev_0209], [ev_0214], [ev_0016]. The 587 s / 9,087-packet capture holds 17 external conversations, none of them to the two endpoints decoded from the data section [ev_0021], [ev_0019]; its DNS extract contains no query for either name, its HTTP extract is GET-only against the ambient Microsoft/OCSP/CRL estate, it shows no regular contact interval, and no SNI was extracted, so 443 destinations are classified by context alone [ev_0234], [ev_0235], [ev_0236], [ev_0017]. The largest conversation, 104.18.19.203:443 (3,666 packets / 229 KB), is attributed by no evidence to the sample and has no tie to these endpoints [ev_0017], [ev_0234]. Both observation windows (600 s run, 587 s capture) exceed the 180 s pre-beacon wait, so non-contact is not a timing artifact of this run [ev_0191], [ev_0227]; the in-sample gates — the process-count 75/50 check and the PEB BeingDebugged check [ev_0088], [ev_0174], [ev_0181], [ev_0225], and the single-instance mutex `runnung` [ev_0019], [ev_0021] — are the better-supported explanation for the channel never being reached. The C2 capability is therefore established at code level only: no session, no tasking reply, no downloaded payload and no exfiltrated body were observed, and 0 files were dropped [ev_0015].

Indicators and attribution. The two endpoints are the indicators of record, and third-party lookups returned malicious verdicts on both domains and both URLs (16/91 and 18/91 for titnovacrion.top and its /live/ path; 19/91 and 21/91 for skinnyjeanso.com and its /live/ path) [ev_0027], [ev_0028], [ev_0034], [ev_0035], [ev_0232], [ev_0233], [ev_0241], [ev_0244]. Family naming attached to the file and to this infrastructure (Latrodectus / IcedId / Ulise) comes from third-party reputation and sandbox classification, not from a C2 session in this run [ev_0018], [ev_0014], [ev_0232], [ev_0241].

packing_obfuscation.body:
**No packer.** The file is an unpacked PE: 5 sections, maximum section entropy 6.48 in .data, 5 imports from only 2 libraries (kernel32.dll, user32.dll), and "packer signatures none" [ev_0004]. The packer scan's `"packed": true` boolean is refuted by its own output: the sole matching rule is `HasRichSignature` @0xb8 (the b'Rich' MSVC linker marker) with no packer name and a "Nothing found" string scan [ev_0139][ev_0145][ev_0251]. That boolean is an artifact of the Rich header and must not be propagated; [ev_0004] stands. What the sample does carry in .data is encrypted configuration, not packed code.

**String obfuscation is the primary mechanism.** All operational text lives in .data as header-validated rolling-XOR blobs: 4-byte seed 0x33629d40, 2-byte length XOR the seed's low 16 bits, then the payload, with keystream byte *i* = `(seed + i + 1) & 0xFF` so the first key byte is 0x41 [ev_0021]. Decoding is performed at run time by routine 0xae78, called from roughly twenty sites; 101 texts decode under the platform's static scheme and 81 of the same set decode by FLOSS emulation [ev_0021][ev_0019], and an independent Ghidra re-derivation reproduced the keystream byte-for-byte [ev_0168]. The consequence is visible in the parsers: 218 strings were recorded but the IOC scan returned none [ev_0005][ev_0006], and the default 31-rule YARA corpus returned 0 hits [ev_0007] — a zero that cannot be read as exculpatory, since the `yara_scan` tool failed twice in this run [ev_0048][ev_0050] and no rule in the corpus targets this family. One token remains unsettled between the two decoders: the header-validated static decode yields `init -zzzz="%s\%s"` @0xfac0 [ev_0021] while emulation yields `init -="%s\%s"` @0x4571 [ev_0019]; both readings are held, and the divergence is confined to one format-string token.

**Dynamic API resolution.** The import directory is complete at 2 DLLs, yet the binary embeds 164 name-hash constants that resolve to functions of wininet, shell32, advapi32, urlmon, shlwapi, iphlpapi, ole32 and ntdll — the full HTTP, filesystem, registry and native-API surface used by the sample [ev_0004][ev_0020]. capa independently matches "resolve function by parsing PE exports" @0x869c and "PEB access" @0x8690 for the walk that finds them, and "contain obfuscated stackstrings" @0x9484, the routine region holding the hashed name table [ev_0008]. We assess this is why the visible import table understates the sample's capabilities, and it is the source of the T1027.007 behaviour rather than any code packer.

**Encrypted content, not encrypted code.** The C2 endpoints [ev_0021] and the entire task vocabulary (`URLS`, `URLS|%d|%s`, `COMMAND`, `CLEARURL`, `ERROR`) [ev_0019] are decoded from the same .data blobs at run time, the RC4 key `"12345"` is itself a decoded blob @0xfd30 and the standard base64 alphabet sits at 0x10160 [ev_0021]; capa corroborates RC4 PRGA @0xcaac, CRC32 @0x6aa4 and FNV @0xc99c [ev_0008]. Application-layer bodies are therefore non-plaintext on the wire. A server-side report for this sample returned an empty ATT&CK mapping while warning that the file "might be obfuscated or encrypted" [ev_0252]; consistent with the above, that zero reflects a heuristic operating on a cleartext layer the sample deliberately does not expose. In summary: no known packer, obfuscation applied to strings, API names and configuration rather than to the code image, and no hidden embedded image in the sections parsed [ev_0004].

evasion_antiforensics.body:
**Encoded strings, decoded just before use.** No operational literal is stored in the clear. All 101 texts the platform recovered from the data sections use one encoding: a 4-byte seed header, a 2-byte length XORed with the seed's low 16 bits, and an xor8 rolling stream over the text [ev_0021]; FLOSS recovered 81 of the same strings through the same routine at 0xae78 [ev_0019]. The disassembly agrees with that scheme: the decoder reads the seed, derives the length, and walks the ciphertext byte by byte into a caller-supplied stack buffer, so a literal is plaintext only in the frame of the statement using it. The stored bytes still read as encoded data — the blob at image-base+0xfa00, for example, is the stored form of "runnung". The two /live/ URLs, the reconnaissance command lines (ipconfig /all, systeminfo, nltest, net view/group, wmic), the install-path fragments and the HTTP body field names therefore never appear as contiguous readable text: the run's IOC extraction returned nothing [ev_0006] and 0 of 31 YARA rules matched [ev_0007].

**Hashed API resolution against a nearly empty import table.** The import directory names five functions from exactly two libraries, kernel32.dll and user32.dll, and that list is complete [ev_0004]. Everything else is obtained through hashes resolved at run time: the file holds 164 constants matching CRC32/FNV hashes of Windows export and module names across kernel32/kernelbase, user32, wininet, shell32, advapi32, urlmon, shlwapi, ole32, iphlpapi and ntdll [ev_0020], with a PEB walk at 0x8690, PE-export parsing at 0x869c, CRC32 hashing at 0x6aa4 and FNV hashing at 0xc99c [ev_0008]. The decompilation captured this run shows the mechanism: sub_0xa59c places 37 crc32_ascii ntdll hashes on the stack as constants — 0xe0762feb (NtAllocateVirtualMemory), 0xb46508b5 (RtlGetVersion), 0xca6b0d7b (NtCreateThread), 0xa5c44c50 (NtQueryInformationProcess), … 0xf675d37d (NtQueryInformationFile) — and resolves each in a loop; all 37 values appear in [ev_0020]. capa records the hash tables at 0x9484 as obfuscated stackstrings and tags this behaviour T1027 [ev_0008]. Nothing in the static import table names either these ntdll primitives or the wininet HTTP calls (InternetOpenW, HttpSendRequestA, InternetReadFile) that are also held as hashes [ev_0020].

**Name and type masquerade; execution through a signed utility.** The artifact is a DLL (IMAGE_FILE_DLL) with four exports, exposed through a routine the reversing tool labels UpdaterTag.dll_extra [ev_0004], and the submission is named as an .exe. The install code builds copy names from "Custom_update" and "Update_%x" and supplies both ".dll" and ".exe" extensions [ev_0019], [ev_0021]; the reversing pass reports the extension is chosen opposite to the payload's real type [ev_0083], [ev_0139]. Execution is proxied through rundll32: the sample's own string table carries "C:\WINDOWS\SYSTEM32\rundll32.exe %s,%s" and a single-argument form [ev_0019], [ev_0021], the sandbox record lists two rundll32.exe processes [ev_0012], Sigma fired on "DLL Call by Ordinal Via Rundll32.EXE" and "Unsigned DLL Loaded by Windows Utility" [ev_0009], and the LOLBIN catalogue records rundll32 (T1218.011) over three command lines [ev_0011]. The file is unsigned [ev_0003] and "Unsigned PE" is among the sandbox's own signatures [ev_0014].

**Rename-then-delete of the sample's own file.** The routine at 0x3a24 acts on the module path cached at image-base+0x10448. It opens that file with CreateFileW(path, 0x10000 /*DELETE*/, 0, NULL, 3 /*OPEN_EXISTING*/, 0x80, NULL), builds a FILE_RENAME_INFO-shaped buffer sized to the wide name plus 0x18 bytes around the decoded string ":wtfbbq" [ev_0019], [ev_0021], and calls SetFileInformationByHandle with class 3 (FileRenameInfo). It then frees the buffer, closes the handle, reopens the same path with DELETE access, passes a one-byte TRUE with class 4 (FileDispositionInfo), and closes again. Class 4 with TRUE is delete-on-close, and the reversing pass reads the function as the uninstall path (command 0xf) that deletes the installed file and the running module before ExitProcess(0) [ev_0093], [ev_0094], [ev_0095], [ev_0184], [ev_0195]. Renaming the file into the colon-prefixed `:wtfbbq` name first, we assess, is intended to take it out of ordinary name-based enumeration and recovery before the delete completes. The sandbox record lists no dropped files [ev_0015], which is consistent with a self-deleting sample, although that record alone does not show the delete executing.

**Packing is not the mechanism.** We do not assess the file as packed: [ev_0004] records no packer signature and the highest section entropy is 6.48 (.data), and the `packed: true` boolean recorded for the sample in this run is driven only by the Rich-header artifact and is unsupported by the PE facts — the reversing pass reached the same conclusion. The hiding in this sample is string encoding, API-name hashing and file-name churn, not wrapped code.

c2_channels.name: HTTPS web-command C2 (check-in, tasking, payload retrieval)
c2_channels.protocol: HTTPS through a WinINet HTTP client. Two endpoints are decoded at run time from a rolling-XOR blob header into a candidate array: https://titnovacrion.top/live/ (@0x10250, referrer 0x69b3) and https://skinnyjeanso.com/live/ (@0x10278, referrer 0x6a1f) [ev_0021][ev_0019]. The client API is resolved by CRC32 name hashing rather than the static IAT: the file holds wininet.dll!InternetOpenW, InternetConnectA, HttpOpenRequestA, HttpSendRequestA, InternetReadFile, InternetCrackUrlA, InternetCloseHandle, InternetSetOptionA, InternetOpenUrlA and InternetOpenUrlW hashes, plus urlmon.dll!URLDownloadToFileW/URLDownloadToFileA, against only 5 static imports [ev_0020]. No IP-literal, DNS-tunnel or non-web transport appears in the decoded configuration; only the two HTTPS endpoints are present [ev_0021][ev_0019].
c2_channels.encryption: Request and reply bodies are RC4 stream-encrypted with the run-time-decoded key "12345" and base64-coded with the standard alphabet ABC...+/ [ev_0021][ev_0019]; capa independently flags 'encrypt data using RC4 PRGA' @0xcaac [ev_0008], and the base64 codec and alphabet install are separately traced [ev_0193]. Transport is TLS; one decompiler locus reads InternetSetOptionA(hRequest, 0x1f, &0x4380, 4), which we assess sets the SECURITY_FLAG_IGNORE_REVOCATION / IGNORE_UNKNOWN_CA / IGNORE_WRONG_USAGE / IGNORE_REDIRECT_TO_HTTPS bits and so weakens certificate and redirect validation - a single-locus reading held at lower confidence [ev_0129][ev_0020].
c2_channels.beacon_format: counter=%d&type=%d&guid=%s&os=%d&arch=%d&username=%s&group=%lu&ver=%d.%d&up=%d&direction=%s (type 2 at install, 1 otherwise, version 1.2; group is FNV-1 of the decoded 'Littlehw' [ev_0008][ev_0021], guid is volume-derived). Reply vocabulary: URLS, URLS|%d|%s, COMMAND, CLEARURL, ERROR, dispatched to a command table mapping ids 2,3,4,0xc-0xf,0x11-0x15 to collectors, downloads, in-memory execution, uninstall and sleep-mode handlers [ev_0019][ev_0021][ev_0169]. Timing: 180 s before first contact, then 450-599 s jittered cycles, lengthened to 1500-2099 s after command 0x13 [ev_0191].
c2_channels.packet_layout: Form-encoded HTTP request with the check-in in the body: verb POST (GET is also present as a decoded verb), header 'Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded', accept '*/*' [ev_0129], User-Agent either 'Mozilla/4.0 (compatible; MSIE 7.0; Windows NT 5.1; Tob 1.1)' or 'curl/7.88.1' [ev_0019][ev_0021]. The body is RC4-then-base64; the reply is read with InternetReadFile and tokenised on CRLF then '|' in the dispatcher [ev_0020][ev_0169]. Download URLs are assembled from the stored C2 entry truncated at '//' plus '/files/' and a token (e.g. 'files/bp.dat', '%d.dat'), with fetched modules written as <tick>.exe / <tick>.dll under the user profile, and one command path allocates RWX memory for a fetched payload and starts a thread on it [ev_0021][ev_0019][ev_0169][ev_0125]. Neither endpoint was reached in this run; the 587 s capture holds 17 external conversations with no regular-interval contact, so the layout is code-level and unexercised [ev_0017].
